sentences.text: 1 The petitioner has filed the claim petition U/Sec. 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against the respondents for seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of the case of the petitioner is as under:
That on 30.06.2024 at about 09.30 p.m, when the petitioner was riding the Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-43-W-4466 on NH-648, near Airline Dhaba, Devanahalli,
Bengaluru, at that time, all of a sudden a Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-40-EJ-1503 came at high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Motor Cycle of the petitioner.

Consequently, he fell down and sustained grievous (SCCH-3)
3 M.V.C.No.6529/2024 injuries and immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Aster hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was treated as inpatient and he was bedridden and under treatment and he has spent nearly Rs.4,00,000/- towards medical and nourishment expenses.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged about 26 years and was working as Supervisor at Sri Lakshmi Chats and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.

Due to accidental injuries, he has to suffer permanent disability and not able to lead a normal life and suffering from shock, pain and physical and mental agony and sustained loss of income, discomfort and amenities.

The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent riding of rider of offending Scooter and in this regard the Devanahalli Traffic Police have registered a case against rider of the offending Motor Cycle.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the said offending vehicle,

are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- to the petitioner together with cost and interest at the rate of 12% p.a.
03.
On service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.6529/2024 counsels, but only the respondent No.1 has filed objections.

04. The respondent No.1 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioner and further denied alleged accident, negligence of the rider of offending Motor Cycle, age, avocation, income of the petitioner, nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner and admits that this respondent has issued Two-wheeler-One year own damage cover bundled with five years liability policy to the vehicle bearing No.KA-40-EJ-1503 and the same is valid as on the date of accident and the liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy and provisions of M.V. Act and contended that the riders of the both Motor Cycles have not holding valid driving licence at the time of accident and the Charge sheet is filed against both riders alleged that both of them have dashed against each other by head on collusion and caused the accident and both of them sustained injuries.
Therefore, the contributory negligence is attributable to the extent of 50% against the petitioner.
The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties.
The compensation claimed is highly excessive, (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.6529/2024 exorbitant.
Hence, pray for dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.1.

sentences.text:
Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following Issues have been framed: -
ISSUES 01.

Whether the petitioner is proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 30.06.2024 at about 9.30 p.m, near Airline Dhaba, Devanahlli,
Bengaluru Rural District, due to rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing registration KA-40-EJ-1503 by its rider as alleged in the petition?
02. Whether respondent No.1 proves that driver has not having valid license?
03. Whether respondent No.1 proves that petitioner Motor Cycle and Insurance Company are necessary parties?
04. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
05.

What Order or Award?
06.
In order to prove his case, the petitioner got himself examined as PW.1 and got examined doctor as PW.2 and got marked 13 documents as Ex.P.1 to 13 and closed his side evidence.
By way of rebuttal, the respondent No.1 got examined its Administrative Officer as RW.1 and got marked 2 documents as Ex.R.1 and 2 and closed its side evidence.

08. Heard both sides.
09.

My findings on the aforesaid Issues are as under:-
Issue No.1 Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.2 In the Negative Issue No.3 In the Affirmative Issue No.4 Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.5 As per final order for the following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1:-
The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the petition averments therein.

In his cross-examination denied the suggestion that accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of the offending Motor Cycle and he sustained injuries in the accident.

sentences.text: He admitted that the road in which he was going is a one way road.

On perusal of the documents,
Ex.P.1 is (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.6529/2024 the FIR registered at Devanahalli Traffic Police against rider of the offending Motor Cycle.
Ex.P.2 is Complaint shows due to rash and negligent riding of the offending Motor Cycle the accident was occurred and due to which the petitioner sustained injuries.

Ex.P.7 is Wound certificate which shows that the petitioner sustained 1) Abrasion present over left knee 3 x 3 cm,
2) Punctured wound present over medial aspect of left leg 2 x 2 cm x bone deep and 3) Compound fracture of both bones (tibia and fibula) of left leg with displacement, out of which injury No.3 is grievous in nature and others are simple in nature.
Ex.P.8 is Discharge summary shows that petitioner sustained type I compound both bone left fracture left side with plan for surgery.
11. The counsel for respondent No.1 argued that this accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner is also contributed to the accident.
To prove its contention, the respondent No.1 got examined its Administrative Officer as RW.1.
In his examination in chief affidavit the RW.1 has reiterated the entire averments of the objections.

Further stated that Devanahalli Traffic police have filed case in Cr.No.136/2024 against one (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.6529/2024 Venkatesh.B.N as accused No.1 and the PW.1 is as accused No.2 and after completion of investigation filed charge sheet for the offences punishable U/sec.279, 337 and 338 of IPC.
Further he has produced copy of Policy as per Ex.R.2, which shows that the policy of the offending Motor Cycle is valid and is in force as on the date of accident.

In the cross examination RW.1 admitted that Police have filed Charge sheet against accused No.1 and as on the date of accident the policy of the vehicle No.KA-40-EJ-1503 is valid and accident occurred at 09.30 p.m on 30.06.2024 and the complaint lodged on 01.07.2024 at 04.00 p.m and the accident occurred on one way road.

12. On perusal of Ex.P.3 and 4 are Sketch and Spot Mahazar showing the place of accident near Airlines Dhaba, Sulibele Road, Devanahalli, Bengaluru, wherein the petitioner's Bullet Bike came from West to East in correct way on the same road, at that time the rider of offending TVS Radeon Bike came from East to West i.e., in one way and in wrong direction i.e., from opposite direction,
came and dashed against the petitioner's Motor Cycle and caused the accident.

On perusal of Ex.P.6 Charge sheet after completion of investigation the Investigation Officer has filed Charge sheet against rider of the offending Motor Cycle as A1 and also against the petitioner as A2, for the offences punishable U/s 279, 337, 338 of IPC and it also appears that due to rash and negligent riding of both vehicles the accident occurred due to head on collision.
In the cross examination PW.1 admitted and stated that, "He was going from Devanahalli towards Sulibele.
While he was traveling from Devanahalli to Hosakote, another motorcyclist came from the opposite direction and caused an accident.
The accident happened at 9:30 p.m.
The road he was driving on was a one-way street.
He didn't go to the accident site.
Both motorcycles were damaged in the accident.
Police have impounded both motorcycles and admits that the Police have filed a final report on him as well and have listed him as the second accused.

The motorcyclist who caused the Kiran Kumar S vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95162269/
4 accident has filed a compensation application, he do not know in which court".

14. Further on perusal of Ex.P.5 IMV report, it discloses:
a) Damages caused to petitioner's vehicle as under:-
 (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.6529/2024  i) Head light assembly damaged  ii) Front left side indicator broken  iii) Handle bar bent and damaged  iv) Fuel tank dent at right side.
b) Damages caused to offending Motor Cycle as under:-
 i) Front wheel mudguard damaged  ii) Front left side crash guard bent iii) Front left side view mirror broken.
It is opined that the occurrence of this accident is not due to any mechanical defects of above motor vehicles.

Though the petitioner was coming on his Bullet Bike in correct way, but in the Charge sheet it is mentioned that the petitioner was riding his bike in negligent manner and caused the accident in head on collision.
Therefore, it is clear that there is a contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner also this accident occurred.
Hence, some contributory negligence taken on the part of the petitioner in the accident, but major negligence is taken on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly, apportion of the negligence on the part of the petitioner is taken at 30% and 70% on the part of the rider of (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.6529/2024 the offending Motor Cycle.
Accordingly, Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered partly in the affirmative.

15. Issues No.2 and 3:- In order to avoid repetition of facts and appreciation of evidence on record,
these issues are taken together for common consideration and discussion.
16. The respondent No.1 has taken specific contention that rider of the offending Motor Cycle was not having valid licence and petitioner has not made owner and insurer of his Motor Cycle as necessary parties.

On perusal of Charge sheet, it is found that in Charge sheet the Investigation Officer has not quoted any sections regarding non-possessing of driving licence by the rider of the offending Motor Cycle and further in the Charge sheet the Investigation Officer has clearly stated that the petitioner who was riding the Motor Cycle in rash and negligent manner and he also contributed for the accident and has filed Charge sheet against petitioner as accused No.2.
But the petitioner has not made owner and insurer of his Motor Cycle as necessary parties.
Hence, the contention of respondent No.1 is acceptable.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered in the negative and Issue No.3 is answered in the affirmative.

Issue No.4:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Road Traffic Accident.

The petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was hale and healthy and was aged about 26 years and was working as Supervisor at Sri Lakshmi Chats and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m and has spent nearly Rs.4,00,000/- towards medical and nourishment expenses.
On account of the accidental injuries, he could not attend to his work and lost his earnings and has become permanent disabled.
18. It is the duty of the petitioner to prove his age, but the petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card to show his exact date of birth.
However, he has produced Ex.P.9 Aadhaar card and Ex.P.10 Driving licence.

Even though the said documents are not authenticated documents for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of any other documents, the same can be relied upon and according to which the date of both of the petitioner is mentioned as 05.11.1998 and the alleged accident was occurred on 30.06.2024 and (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.6529/2024 hence it appears that as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner is 26 years.
Therefore, considering the said document, this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 26 years.

As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 26 to 30 is '17'.

sentences.text: 19. With regard to avocation and income of the petitioner is concerned, he has not placed any materials before the tribunal.

Therefore, in the absence of evidence regarding his avocation and income, this tribunal has to go by the Lok-Adalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2024 to be taken as Rs.16,500/- p.m. Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the petitioner is at Rs.16,500/- and it is multiplied by 12.
20.

According to the evidence of PW.2, the Doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his chief examination that petitioner sustained type I compound fracture both bones (tibia and fibula) left leg and he has assessed (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.6529/2024 permanent residual physical disability of about 31.66% of left lower limb, which is about 15.83% of whole body and he has produced OPD slip and X-ray as per Ex.P.12 and 13.

In his cross-examination he admits that he has not treated the petitioner personally and he has consulted the treated doctor and admits that except the Wound certificate and Discharge summary, he has not seen the follow-up records and that fractures are united and denied to the suggestion that he has assess the disability at higher side and this kind of disability does not arise and admits that he has mentioned one more surgery for removal of implants and that he has assessed physical disability and not functional disability.

However, considering the evidence of PW.2, nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and medical records, this tribunal has assessed functional disability of the petitioner at 1/3rd i.e.,
10.55%.

Therefore, the loss of future income works out as under:
Rs.16,500/- x 12 x 17 x 10.55%/100 = Rs.3,55,113/-.

sentences.text: Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:-
The petitioner has produced Discharge summary of Aster CMI hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was admitted as inpatient for (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.6529/2024 04 days.
During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount towards attendant charges, special diet, transportation and nutrition.
Therefore, considering the duration of treatment, towards attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.

22. Pain and sufferings:- As per Ex.P.7 Wound certificate and as per evidence of PW.2 doctor and as per X-ray and on account of accidental injuries, petitioner would have undergone pain and agony and he has sustained grievous injuries.

Accordingly with regard to fractures suffered by him in the accident, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/-
under this head.
23. Loss of income during laid up period:-

As already discussed above, the petitioner has not produced any documents regarding avocation and income and this tribunal has assessed the notional income at Rs.16,500/- p.m and he was admitted in the hospital for 04 days as inpatient.

Considering the nature of injuries, treatment taken,
duration of his stay in hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least two months.
Thus, taking into account the notional income (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.6529/2024 of the petitioner, this tribunal award a sum of Rs.33,000/- (Rs.16,500 x 2) under this head.
24. Medical expenses:- The petitioner has produced entire Medical bills as per Ex.P.11 for Rs.3,03,994/-.
To disprove the medical bills, the respondent No.1 has not produced any documents nor any evidence.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.3,03,994/- under this head.

25. Loss of future amenities and unhappiness:- Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness, the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness.
26. Future medical expenses:-
According to doctor PW.2 the petitioner is advised to undergo another operation for removal of implants from left tibia.
But the doctor has not stated about actual cost of surgery and has not produced any estimation regarding future medical expenses.
Hence, under the facts and circumstances of the case, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-

As discussed in the Issue No.1, this tribunal already held that due to contributory negligence of the petitioner and rider of offending Motor Cycle this accident occurred, hence the petitioner's negligence part is taken at 30% and the rider of offending vehicle negligence is taken at 70% respectively.

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:
Rs.8,12,107/- - 2,43,632/- (30%) = Rs.5,68,475/-.

Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,68,475/- with interest at the (SCCH-3) 18 M.V.C.No.6529/2024 rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.

29. Regarding liability:- On service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared and respondent No.1 has filed objections and contested the matter, but not lead evidence to disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove its contention.
On the date of accident policy was in force.
Hence, respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay above said compensation amount.
Respondent No.1 Insurance Company is directed to deposit above said compensation amount within two months from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.4 partly in affirmative.
30. Issue No.5:-

In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 to 4, I proceed to pass the following:- -
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,68,475/-
(Rupees Five lakhs sixty eight thousand four hundred and seventy five only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
